q: How much CO2 does denim washing add per garment?
title: Denim washing CO2 per garment
short: Add the laundry's boiler fuel, dryer fuel and electricity for a month, multiply each by its emission factor, and divide by the pieces washed. Heavy stone and enzyme washes take far more heat and machine time than a rinse, so split by wash recipe where you can. Dryers often use most of the heat.
audience: Denim laundries and garment exporters in Bengaluru, Ahmedabad and Tiruppur

sections.h: What goes into a laundry's figure
ul: Boiler fuel for hot water and steam: PNG, LPG, coal, briquettes or furnace oil.
Tumble dryer fuel, if dryers are gas-fired rather than steam-heated.
Electricity for washers, extractors, dryers, laser and ozone machines, compressors and the ETP.
Chemicals, enzymes and pumice are Scope 3 purchased goods; add them if the buyer asks for a cradle-to-gate figure.

p: Pieces washed is a fair divisor only when recipes are similar. Otherwise give each recipe a weight from metered steam or gas per batch, or from machine minutes times load, and share the month's emissions by weighted pieces.
Re-measure the weights when you change a recipe, for example when ozone fading replaces a bleach step.

Laser and ozone finishing replace hand scraping, potassium permanganate spray and some bleaching baths. They cut water, chemicals and hot rinse steps, but they add electricity. Count both sides: lower boiler fuel per piece, higher kWh per piece at 0.710 kg CO2 each.

Report laundry per piece as its own stage. Buyers add it to fabric, stitching and freight, and a combined factory figure hides where the heat goes. If the laundry is a jobworker, it is your Scope 3; ask for its monthly bills and wash counts.

example.title: Worked example: one month at a denim laundry
lines: Boiler PNG: 8,000 scm x 2.05 = 16,400 kg CO2
Dryer LPG: 6,000 kg x 2.98 = 17,880 kg CO2
Total: 69,780 kg CO2 for 100,000 pieces = 0.70 kg CO2 per piece on average
By recipe: 40,000 stone and enzyme washes at weight 3, 60,000 rinses at weight 1, so 180,000 weighted pieces
69,780 / 180,000 = 0.388 kg per weighted piece; stone wash 1.16 kg, rinse 0.39 kg per piece
example.note: Recipe weights are illustrative; take them from your own batch metering.

senseible: Senseible reads the laundry's PNG, LPG, coal and electricity invoices (Scope 1 at IPCC 2006 defaults, Scope 2 at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh) and keeps chemical purchases in the Scope 3 evidence trail. Product reports are self-declared drafts; wash counts and recipe weights come from your production register.
